how: Both opens succeed at 0 ms (no latency, libs/visa/simulation.md 2), and each `scpi.wait_complete` sends `*OPC?` at 0 ms, answered from `commands`, which wins over the simulator's own answer (simulation.md 2 and 4, points 3 and 4). In `scpi.wait_complete` (libs/scpi/wait_complete.lcf; spec A.3): SIM::DEV0 answers `done`, which `string.to_i32` cannot read, so it fails with `string.parse` and its `value` takes the default 0 (spec A.2, 7.2); SIM::DEV1 answers `0`, the i32 0. Either way `core.ne(value, 1)` is true, and `errors.raise_if`, whose `err` is `e1`, `none` here, runs and makes a `scpi.unexpected_response`; the error of `string.to_i32` only orders it (`after:`) and is dropped. `raise_if` has no code, so the code is 0 (spec 7.1), and its message is the `string.format` of the library, a string field shown as its text alone (spec 5.4; escapes of 14.1): `*OPC? answered "done", not 1` and `*OPC? answered "0", not 1`. Its origin is the node `e3`, named by its first output, line 17 of the library file, under the caller nodes `a2` (line 14) and `b2` (line 16) of `wait_on_two` (commands.md 5 and 8). Each `visa.close` is `always`, closes its session and passes its error on (spec 7.2), so nothing is left open. `errors.merge(e3, e6)` makes the error of SIM::DEV0, its first argument, the main error, and puts that of SIM::DEV1 in its `others`, without its own `others` (spec 7.4; commands.md 5). `err` holds it, so the status is `error` and `error` repeats it (spec 7.5, 8.2; commands.md 7). Resources in code point order of their names (commands.md 7); the run ends at 0 ms. The check finds nothing (spec 7.5, 8.1: every error output is wired, and the two sessions are on two resources).
